main_with_engine_kept.rule: main gate + the kept engine part (BSBatchRenderer + BSShader prepare/update per draw, mix_hi, IPC 0.6 at 1.02 GHz)

summary.per_draw_us_rule: CPU per draw over a whole frame (fixed per-frame costs included), mix_lo and mix_hi: lo = IPC 1.0 at 1.785 GHz, hi = gate = IPC 0.6 at 1.02 GHz. native = front (StateTracker, translator, packet build, sort, encode) + deko3d recording (nxgpu.c record + libdeko3d); nine = st/nine without any pipe driver (nouveau's validation and push-buffer work is NOT in it), x86-64 count scaled to AArch64
summary.frame_ms_rule: mix_hi (3710 draws) at 1.02 GHz for hi/gate (IPC 0.6; main adds the store term), mix_lo (1490 draws) at 1.785 GHz IPC 1.0 for lo. main = packet build (engine-side StateTracker + Renderer::Render); render = Frame::Finish + deko3d recording

assumptions.gate_value: gate = hi = IPC 0.6 at 1.02 GHz, mix_hi (+ memory term on main)

summary.targets_budget_fraction_rule: THE GATE FIELD. Per target (30/45/60 fps = 33.3/22.2/16.7 ms): '1.02'/'1.785' = worst CPU renderer thread (mix_hi, IPC 0.6, store term) / budget; 'gpu_<cfg>' = GPU model (mix_hi, issue efficiency 0.6) / budget; 'frame_<cfg>' = max(CPU at 1.02 GHz, GPU) / budget for the gate configs docked_720p and handheld_720p (dynamic resolution off). <= 1.0 passes. CPU covers the renderer only (engine not counted); '1.02_with_engine_kept' = the worst CPU thread with the kept engine part on main; 'd3d9_path_main_1.02' = the D3D9 fallback's main thread (engine path + st/nine, no driver) / budget, for comparison
summary.targets_rule: CPU verdict: max(main hi, render hi) of mix_hi at IPC 0.6 (the low IPC bound decides) <= 33.3/22.2/16.7 ms; covers the renderer only (engine update/cull/accumulation not measured); GPU time is a separate estimate (gpu.targets)

frame_budget.rule: owner: 60 fps for the whole frame at 720p handheld; the gate reads targets_budget_fraction['60']

summary.engine_d3d9_path_source: MEASURED (static path count) on the AArch64 ILP32 prepared objects, render/native/perf/engine_path.py; replaces the assumption of PERF.md §5 / RENDER_PERF.md §3.7

nine.method: x86-64 callgrind, same .nxd3d stream through both paths: native front (null backend, -O2) vs Gallium Nine 20.1 st/nine (+cso, u_upload, util, libc it calls; release -O3) with every call into softpipe (state objects, draw module, rasterizer, flush) excluded (perf/cg_split.py); CSMT off (softpipe lacks PIPE_CAP_BUFFER_MAP_PERSISTENT_COHERENT); the engine's D3D9 redundancy filter (NiDX9RenderState) modelled and counted on the Nine side
nine.nine_a64_estimate_rule: x86-64 Nine count x (native a64 / native x86-64): assumes Nine's code has the same instruction ratio between the ISAs as the front; not measured
nine.with_engine_rule: D3D9 path per frame = engine_d3d9_path total (d3d9 path + kept) + st/nine A64 estimate; native = front + deko3d recording + the kept engine part; nouveau still excluded

gpu.model:
Per DKSH: registers (DkshProgramHeader.num_gprs), Maxwell instructions (code words that are not scheduling words,
not uam's NOP / "BRA $" padding), and from uam's TGSI (-t): static instruction count, texture instructions, and a
dynamic estimate (the dynamic light loop of lit*.frag run LIGHTS times: the for-loops with a non-literal bound
after the preprocessor; every other TGSI loop is a compiled switch and runs once; both arms of every IF are counted,
so branchy epilogues are upper bounds). maxwell_dyn = maxwell_static x tgsi_dyn / tgsi_static. Each family is
costed with the fragment shaders nx::Renderer binds for it (bound_shaders: static light and epilogue permutations,
weighted by the stream's alpha-test / fog mix), not the runtime base shader.

Scene model (MODEL below, every number is copied into the JSON): per family, covered pixels = target pixels x
coverage x overdraw; fragment time = pixels x max(ALU: maxwell_dyn / 256 lanes, TEX: tex x TEX_COST / 16 TMUs,
ROP: 1 / 16, depth-only 1 / 32, 64-bit colour 1 / 8) / clock, ALU and TEX divided by an issue efficiency (EFF: 1.0 and
0.6 give the lo/hi estimate); ALU slots count fp16x2 instructions at half cost (FP16_RATE); DRAM bytes per pixel
from the family's render-target format (TARGET_FORMATS, colour x2 when blending), depth traffic x Z_COMPRESS and
TEX_BYTES per texture fetch; presets (PRESETS) give target size, shadow map and reflection size per config; vertex time = draws x vertices x vs maxwell_dyn / 256 / clock; frame
time = max(sum over families, DRAM traffic / (25.6 GB/s x efficiency)). No caches, no early-z rejection benefit
beyond the overdraw factor, no cross-family overlap, no CPU/GPU sync stalls.

assumptions.real019_source: carried from the previous report.json (sdp2dksh not built in this run)

backend_record.method:
Counted per frame: dkCmdBufClear + dkCmdBufAddMemory + record() (stream decode, state-block replay, every dkCmdBuf*
call, dkCmdBufFinishList, dkQueueSubmitCommands, swapchain acquire/present bookkeeping). The libnx services under
it are stand-ins that return at once (perf/dk/stubs.c): the kernel/ioctl time of a real submit is not counted.

assumptions.measured_frame: last (warm caches, same draws as frame 0)
assumptions.cache_misses: not modelled by the counter; the IPC range is meant to cover L1 misses of the front's tables, the hi estimate of the main thread adds a streaming-store term (bytes_per_draw_memory_term / store_gbs)
assumptions.a64_counter: Unicorn UC_HOOK_BLOCK, size/4 per basic block; ILP32 guest -O2 -mtune=cortex-a57; stream decoder subtracted (dry run)
assumptions.not_counted: engine update, cull, accumulation; skinning palettes; dynamic vertex data. The engine's own D3D9 draw path is now measured: engine_d3d9_path (it was assumed 1-3 k instructions per draw)
assumptions.engine_d3d9_path: MEASURED (static path count) on the AArch64 ILP32 prepared objects, render/native/perf/engine_path.py; replaces the assumption of PERF.md §5 / RENDER_PERF.md §3.7

engine_d3d9_path.source: MEASURED (static path count) on the AArch64 ILP32 prepared objects, render/native/perf/engine_path.py; replaces the assumption of PERF.md §5 / RENDER_PERF.md §3.7

replaced_assumption.text: engine's own per-draw work before the device: 1-3 k instructions [E] (PERF.md §5); 10-20 us/draw (RENDER_PERF.md §3.7, mostly this side)

engine_d3d9_path.per_draw_instr_rule: exp = static expectation over the hot path (branch rules and loop trips of the spec: mix_hi draw-weighted RS / stage / constant counts, 81 % of render states redundant); lo / hi = the same with the spec's low / high sensitivity (redundancy 90 % / 60 %, 1 / 4 state-group entries per pass); path_min / path_max = shortest / longest path, bounds only
engine_d3d9_path.limits: static count (no execution): branch probabilities are rules, not measurements; 69 indirect calls stay unresolved (mostly geometry/skin getters and the strip path) and count their call only; the shader class is the lit one (shadow-light) for the BSShader virtuals; device calls end at our D3D9 front (counted in §1); per-frame fixed engine work (BeginFrame/EndFrame, target groups) is not in it
